text:
Thomas Harley is 25, an Olympian for Canada last winter, and Dallas is leaning on him harder than ever. He averages 25.5 minutes a night and has topped 28 in three of his last six games, including 30.9 in a 2-1 win over Florida. He has 14 points in 20 games, 12 of them assists.

The scoring pace, 1.65 points per 60 minutes, sits at the top of our range for him, so some cooling would be normal. The five-on-five numbers are the better news. Dallas gets about 55% of the shot attempts and expected goals with him on the ice (expected goals measure the quality of chances), close to 5 points better than without him, and he has blocked 46 shots.

That matters because last season told a different story. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level in 2025-26, with opponents getting more chances when he played (bottom 10% of defensemen). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking showed the attacking side: 52% of his entries carried in and 28% of his shots off the rush, against 17% for a typical defenseman. Watch whether the defensive gains hold up under all these minutes.
headline: Harley is carrying Dallas' blue line minutes
